intended_object: The germ at x of a scalar function f analytic at x, seen as an element of the ring 𝒪ₓ of analytic germs at x (from the docstring and the definition of `analyticGermRing` just above it).
explanation:
`analyticGermRing x` is the subring of `Germ (𝓝 x) ℂ` made of the germs of functions analytic at x. `germ f hf` is the element of that subring whose underlying value is the filter germ `↑f`. The membership proof uses f itself as the witness, together with `hf`. This is exactly the usual germ of f at x in 𝒪ₓ.

The setting is a finite-dimensional complex normed space with values in ℂ. That is the standard setting of several complex variables, where 𝒪ₓ is studied. The library uses the definition there for results such as "𝒪ₓ is a local Noetherian UFD" and the Weierstrass theorems, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has `Filter.Germ`, which this definition builds on, but no separate definition of the analytic-germ element. The library's own `SeveralComplexVariables.analyticGermSubring` is the same ring by `rfl`, but it is not part of Mathlib.
